title: Better Resource Monitor vs Eul
description: Eul stopped getting updates and burns CPU on Apple Silicon. Here is what I switched to and why.
heading: Better Resource Monitor vs Eul
intro: Eul stopped getting updates years ago. On M-series Macs it has known high CPU usage, no fixes coming, and GPU monitoring that depends on private APIs which break between macOS releases. After dealing with that for a while I wrote Better Resource Monitor. GPU data comes from the IOAccelerator API, the whole thing stays inside the App Sandbox, and it measures under 0.1% CPU on Apple Silicon.

sections.heading: Maintenance matters for system tools
sections.body: A menu bar monitor touches IOKit, SMC, and whatever Apple rearranges each fall. Eul's last meaningful commit was years ago. No macOS Sequoia fixes, no Apple Silicon tuning, no security patches. I test against every macOS beta and push fixes before the public release ships.

sections.heading: CPU usage on Apple Silicon
sections.body: On M-series Macs, Eul's CPU usage climbs noticeably. Nobody is maintaining it, so that will never get fixed. The Rust core in Better Resource Monitor keeps the whole app under 0.1% CPU by skipping the work that causes the overhead (SMC helpers, constant sensor polling).

sections.heading: GPU data without private APIs
sections.body: Eul's App Store version ships with limited features because it uses private, undocumented APIs for GPU data. Those can silently break on any macOS point release. I read GPU utilization through IOAccelerator, the public IOKit interface. Same data, stable across updates, full GPU monitoring on the App Store.

cta: If Eul was working for you before it stopped getting updates, [Better Resource Monitor](https://apps.apple.com/app/better-resource-monitor/id6758237306) covers the same ground. Source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/alexx855/better-resource-monitor) if you want to look before you install.
